README: The sound sheet. Read Topics/Explainer/SOUND.md first. Times are cues and words, never seconds. Then: python3 scripts/sound.py build why-does-bread-cost-more-every-year

sections.why: The question, the loaf, and the same loaf when your mom was your age: something ordinary, and something odd about it.
The cause, step by step, in a village small enough to count. Facts, one after another: the steady step of the topic.
Up and out to the real world: bigger, busier, the same thing happening all the time.
A hundred years down, where it went wrong fast. A pulse that will not stop, under the press and the price nobody could pay.
Home, and now it makes sense. It stays in this mood through your chest and the subscribe line: never a new tune for the last three seconds.

beds.why: A bare stone island a long way down: wind, and no birds.

sfx.why: The question mark over his head: there on the first frame.
The flight in from the whole stall to the kid: a whoosh as long as the flight.
The shrug.
Past his shoulder to the loaf.
The tag swings round to face us. Every tag in the film turns with this sound.
The first coin lands under the loaf, 0.2 s after it is let go (dropped() in kit.tsx).
The second coin, beside it: a little higher.
Over the edge of the island and down.
Down into the past: the whistle goes the way the camera goes.
Her tag swings round, as today's did.
Her one coin lands. The same coin sound, lower: an older coin.
Back, fast, until both stalls are in the frame.
The two loaves hop together, a beat after 'bread'.
The two ovens flare together.
The two tags swell: the one thing that is not the same.
The arrow grows from the one up to the two. Up is dearer, in this film.
The flight down and west to the village.
A village has a bell. One stroke, small, on its name.
Round to the front of the rack.
Ten loaves pop on to the rack one after another (0.05 s apart): one count that runs up, not ten pops.
Ten coins drop in two rows at the foot of the rack. Short and low: the end of the sentence ('to buy them with') is quiet, and a longer spill covered it.
In, and round to the left.
The coins fly up, each to its own loaf, for 0.8 s: four coins going up the scale stand for ten.
The big tag over the rack pops: a price is fixed. One.
Back and round, with sky over the rack.
Ten more coins come down out of the sky.
They land where the first ten waited.
To the baker.
He counts the rack with his head, and each loaf hops as he gets to it.
The bubble: 10. The same ten.
The whole rack again.
The ten new coins fly up: the same run of coins as the first time.
The big tag spins once.
It comes round as 2: the same stamp as the first price.
The farmer and the baker shake their heads, as the camera pushes slowly in: no more bread than before.
Two heads still shaking, a robe and a straw hat: the only things that move while the camera closes in.
Every loaf comes apart down the middle: half a loaf over each coin.
Up and out to the west.
A long climb through open sky.
A bundle of notes hops from the tray to the printer's roof: slowly, here.
A loaf hops out of the oven on to its stack.
And one more bundle.
In to the two machines.
The printer speeds up: nine bundles in 2.3 s (money in scene5.tsx).
The stack of money runs up past the stack of bread.
Loaves hop out too, but not as often.
Down to the loaf in front of the stage.
The balloon takes a breath and the price goes up a step: 3.
And again: 4.
And again: 5. The scenes start this step 0.2 s before 'up'.
The last, biggest breath.
The word is on the balloon: the thing has its name.
The longest flight of the film: a hundred years down.
The floor goes out from under you.
The press, as big as a house: iron.
It prints as fast as it can be cranked (16 notes a second in scene5.tsx): a flutter of paper.
The notes pour off the edge of the island and the wind takes them.
Along the edge to the loaf.
One loaf, on top of its plinth.
Its price starts to unroll: 200.
A row of zeros.
Another.
And the last row lands, 0.22 s after 'billion' begins: 200,000,000,000. The one big hit of the film, on the number that is its surprise.
Home: up out of 1923, past the stall where your mom paid one.
Up is later: the whistle climbs with the camera, as it fell going down.
The loaf of the first ten seconds, unchanged: the right answer starts here.
Two stacks of coins rise at the ends of the counter.
Today's loaf comes apart, as the village's ten did: half over each coin.
The answer is given. After the word, in the breath before the next line.
Along the island to your own door.
The lid.
It is full.
A loaf goes from the stack beside it.
And another.
And another: each one lower. Nothing has left the chest.
In to you, as you jump clear of the chest with the sign.
The red sign goes up over your head.
The tag on it swings round: the same sound as the first tag of the film.
0. The subscribe line, after its last word.
